framework_rationale: The submission imports only tensorcircuit as a quantum framework (alongside standard scientific/ML libraries numpy, scipy, jax, and optax) and performs the core quantum circuit construction, state evolution, Hamiltonian expectation evaluation, and string-order expectation measurements using tensorcircuit (tc.QuditCircuit, c.x, c.unitary, tc.backend.expm, tc.templates.measurements.operator_expectation, c_fin.expectation, and tensorcircuit runtime context managers).
cheating_rationale: There are no hardcoded outputs, hidden-answer accesses, test/reward tampering, or evaluator exploits. The code builds the Hamiltonian from the config parameters, initializes variational parameters from the seeded Gaussian distribution, runs the full 500-step Adam optimization loop, and measures the final energy density and string correlators directly on the optimized variational circuit.
fidelity_rationale: The implementation faithfully matches all mathematical and algorithmic details of Problem 11: the spin-1 operators in the {|+1>, |0>, |-1>} basis, the bilinear-biquadratic Hamiltonian with single-ion anisotropy, the Neel initial state prepared via two shift X gates on odd sites, the 5-layer brickwork ansatz (Rz-Ry-Rz single-site rotations, even-bond and odd-bond two-qutrit entangling gates with the fixed beta*(Si·Sj)^2 term and 3*n_sites + 2*(n_sites-1) parameters per layer), seeded Gaussian initialization, exact max_steps Adam updates with pre-update energy density logging, post-update final energy density evaluation, and the three spin-1 string correlators at (0,11), (1,10), and (2,9).
implementation_error_rationale: No implementation errors were found. Matrix exponentiation, analytical spin-1 Ry/Rz parameterization, sparse BCSR Hamiltonian construction, JAX/Optax scan optimization, and TensorCircuit qudit circuit expectations are all consistent and produce physically accurate results.
